senses.gloss: m. (עכל, cmp. אוּכְלָא II a. כְּלָה) ‘Ukhla, a small measure of capacity (also a weight).
units: <cite ref="Bava Batra 90a:1">Ib. 90ᵃ</cite> <he>וכמה היא ע׳ אחד משמונה ברובע</he> (ed. <he>מחמשה ברביע</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. to 89ᵇ note 400) and how much is an ‘Ukhla? One-eighth (fifth) of a fourth of a Kab.

<cite ref="Sotah 8b">Sot. 8ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 3:1">Tosef. ib. III, 1</cite> (missing in ed. Zuck.; Y. ib. I, 17ᵃ <cite ref="A00529"><he>אוכלא</he></cite>); <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 9:24">Num. R. s. 9</cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 29a:9">Erub. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>ע׳ תבלין</he> an ‘U. of spices (v. <cite ref="K00690"><he>כְּלָה</he></cite>).—Pl. <he>עוּכְלֵי</he>.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 85b:4">B. Bath. 85ᵇ</cite> <he>מחו לה מאה ע׳ עוכלא</he> they struck (defeated) that opinion with a hundred measures against one (a hundred arguments against for one in favor of it; Rashi: with a hundred strokes with a lash to which the weight of an ‘Ukhla was attached); <cite ref="Ketubot 53a:6">Keth. 53ᵃ</cite> <he>דאמינא כמאן דקא מחו וכ׳</he> for I may adopt the opinion of him who said, they struck &c.
